entries.content:
Read the file and traced the poller. No code changed.

## Findings

**Root cause: the session line in the log has no reset clause, and the parser requires one.**

The logged screen is complete (the excerpt in `desktop/src/actions/agent/claude_usage_diagnostics.js` keeps the last 12 lines / 600 chars and prefixes `…` when it truncates — there is no `…`, so those three lines are all Claude printed):

```
Current session: 0% used
Current week (all models): 1% used · resets Sep 13, 6:59pm (Europe/Brussels)
```

Claude omits `· resets …` for the session window when the session is at 0%. Both `WINDOW_PATTERNS` entries in `desktop/src/actions/agent/claude_usage_parsing.js:7` make everything from `·` onward mandatory, so the `five_hour` pattern misses, `parseClaudeUsageOutput` throws `Missing Claude usage window`, and the fallback `parseTerminalUsageOutput` also misses because it wants the boxed layout (heading `Current session` on its own line, then a `Resets …` line). Result is `null` → `stdout-unparsed`. I confirmed this by running the parser on the exact logged text: it returns `null`, and returns a full two-window payload as soon as a reset clause is added to the session line.

**Second, independent fault: the pty fallback never answers.**

Every `pty` record is `pty-host-deadline` at ~57.2 s, which is exactly the stdout attempt (~2.2 s) plus the host budget in `claude_usage_terminal_host.js` (30 s ready + 20 s report + 5 s grace). The worker has its own earlier deadlines in `claude_usage_terminal.js` — 30 s ready, then 20 s report — so it should always reply at ~30 s or ~50 s with `pty-no-ready-marker` or `pty-report-timeout`, and never let the host deadline win. It never does, on any of the twelve polls. The screen it saw is lost too, because `hostDeadline` is built by `inconclusiveResult`, which carries an empty `screenExcerpt`. Most likely the worker blocks inside `killProcess()` → node-pty's ConPTY teardown on Windows, which is exactly the native hazard the out-of-process design was built for, but I cannot confirm that from the logs alone — the excerpt is empty precisely where the evidence would be.

**Downstream constraint that shapes the fix.** A parsed window with no reset time cannot simply be passed through: `claude_runtime_service.js:8` drops any window whose `resetsAt` is not finite, `normalizeWindows` then rejects the whole payload; `app/src/services/agents/claude_rate_limit_service.ts:29` rejects it again in the renderer; and `usage_metrics_service.js:236` returns `null` for the *entire* snapshot if any window fails, including the `five_hour` one it goes on to discard (only `weekly` is recorded).

**Minor:** the reset time alternates between `6:59pm` and `7pm` across polls, so `resetsAt` jitters by 60 s. `sameWindows` treats that as a change and republishes the snapshot; `sameAccountWindow`'s tolerance is `<= 60_000`, so it holds — but only exactly.

## How I'd fix it

1. Make the reset clause optional in both `WINDOW_PATTERNS` entries (`(?:\s*·\s*resets …)?`), and have `parseClaudeUsageOutput` yield `resetsAt: null` when the clause is absent instead of throwing. Same for `parseTerminalWindow`, which currently requires a `Resets` line.
2. Carry nullable `resetsAt` through the Claude path the way the Codex path already does: `codex_runtime_service.js` uses `window.resetsAt ?? null`, `electron_codex_runtime_bridge.ts` types it `number | null`, and `codex_rate_limit_details.tsx:31` renders `Reset unknown`. So: allow `null` in `claude_runtime_service.normalizeWindow`, in `electron_claude_runtime_bridge`'s type, in `claude_rate_limit_service.validSnapshot` and `firstResetTime` (skip nulls when taking the minimum), and in `claude_rate_limit_details.tsx`'s `formatReset`.
3. In `usage_metrics_service.claudeAccountWindows`, normalize only the `weekly` calculation window rather than every window, so a session window without a reset time no longer discards the whole snapshot.
4. Separately, for the pty path: instrument the worker before changing it — log a record when each worker-side deadline fires and attach the screen to `hostDeadline` — so the next run says whether the worker is hanging in teardown or never getting that far. If it is the ConPTY kill, the fix is to resolve the promise before killing rather than after.

Tests to add alongside: a `claude_usage_parsing.test.mjs` case with the exact three-line screen from this report, and a `usage_metrics_service` case where the session window has a null reset and the weekly row is still recorded.

Want me to implement this?

 * Traces the stages of a pty poll from inside the worker, where a failure that never reports back

 */
function logUsagePollStage(stage, detail = {}) {
    console.warn(CLAUDE_USAGE_LOG_TAG, { stage, timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), ...detail });

    logUsagePollStage,
    usageScreenExcerpt,""")
io.open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8',newline='\n').write(s)

Done. (`agent_runner_state.test.mjs` in that list is pre-existing WIP from your tree, not mine.)

## What changed

**Parser — `desktop/src/actions/agent/claude_usage_parsing.js`**
- The reset clause is now an optional group shared by both window patterns (`RESET_CLAUSE_SOURCE`), so `Current session: 0% used` parses and yields `resetsAt: null`. `resetTimestamp` returns `null` when the clause is absent.
- When a redraw shows the same window twice, a line carrying a reset clause now beats a bare one; before, the first line simply won.
- `parseTerminalWindow` stops its search at the next heading, so a boxed window without a `Resets` line no longer borrows the next window's reset time. It also accepts a missing reset line.

**Nullable reset carried through, mirroring the existing Codex path**
- `claude_runtime_service.js` accepts `resetsAt: null` instead of rejecting the whole payload.
- `electron_claude_runtime_bridge.ts` types it `number | null`; `claude_rate_limit_service.ts` accepts null in `validSnapshot` and skips nulls in `firstResetTime`, so staleness is scheduled off the window that does have a reset time.
- `claude_rate_limit_details.tsx` renders `Reset unknown`, the same wording the Codex popover uses.

**Metrics — `usage_metrics_service.js`:** `claudeAccountWindows` normalizes only the `weekly` calculation window, so a session window without a reset no longer discards the weekly measurement.

**pty instrumentation:** added `logUsagePollStage` to `claude_usage_diagnostics.js`, and traced the failure paths only — both deadlines in `claude_usage_terminal.js` log the screen and bracket the `killProcess()` call, and the worker brackets its `postMessage`. A stage logged without its follow-up will name the step that hangs, and the screen behind a `pty-host-deadline` is no longer lost.

## Verification

- Parser now returns the full two-window payload for the exact screen in the bug report; the existing formats still parse. New tests cover the logged screen, the boxed layout with the session reset line removed, and the bare-then-full redraw.
- New tests for the runtime service (null reset kept), the metrics service (weekly row still written), the rate-limit service (expires on the window with a reset), and the status popover (`Reset unknown`).
- `npm run typecheck` clean; ESLint clean on all touched files.
- Desktop suite: 1043 passed, 4 failed. App suite: 3297 passed, 23 failed. None are mine — they are in `config.test.mjs`, `agent_profiles_parity.test.mjs`, `action_agent_executor.test.mjs`, `agent_profiles.node.test.ts`, `agent_selection.node.test.ts` and `diff_service.node.test.ts`, all about model/profile config and project paths, in files I did not touch. Every Claude usage, rate-limit and metrics test passes.
